answers.explanation: It's cheap and needs no extra hardware, just several records.
Plain DNS has no idea a server is down, and caches keep the address until the TTL runs out. That's why real load balancers health-check.
Two views of one zone: internal and external.
Anycast uses BGP from chapter 6 to pick the nearest copy.
Each site announces the same prefix with BGP; routers choose the closest by AS path and policy.
With anycast, `a.root-servers.net` is one address answered from many sites.
Each attacking machine's traffic goes to its own nearest site, so the load spreads out.
The server picks the answer by location, sending each user to a nearby data center.
